subject: Using FA icons in DataTables, without risking html injection attacks

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Using FA icons in DataTables, without risking html injection attacks
parts:
If html injection is a concern (and escape=F was dangerous), is there a recommended approach to show FA icons?  Is reducing the number of columns showing HTML (by passing their names or index position) the only mitigation?

Background: My Shiny report has Font Awesome icons included in the DataTable (see the attached image).  After upgrading Shiny from 0.10.2 to 0.11.0, the HTML in the cells is rendered only when escape=FALSE (as documented in the NEWS, and Issue #627).  The table doesn't reflect any user input, so I don't think there's a security concern for the current report.  But I'd like to know in general.

If it helps, the report is here http://shiny.ouhsc.edu/TfcbtPublic/Shiny/TherapistProgress/ (select a therapist tag, such as '27vk'), and the source code is here: https://github.com/OuhscBbmc/TfcbtPublic/tree/master/Shiny/TherapistProgress.

Also, should the new escape parameter be mentioned in the Shiny 0.11 migration notes?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Using FA icons in DataTables, without risking html injection attacks
parts: Yes, in this case passing the negative index positions is the recommended approach for sure.
